title: Stage gameplay tool mutations until audited turn acceptance
description:
Problem
The native Agent SDK MCP path can execute state-mutating tools during a candidate turn before the turn auditor accepts the model response. In session-mqkis411-rlsh20, the player asked a read-style question ("What am I equipped with?"), the model executed inventory mutation tools, the auditor rejected the candidate, and the retry then failed due to provider session limit. The user-facing message said the input was not applied, but some tool calls had already returned applied=true.

This creates a dangerous state-integrity gap:
- candidate model response executes mutating tools
- auditor rejects the response or retry fails
- user is told the turn was not applied
- state mutations from the rejected candidate may still persist

Goal
Make gameplay tool side effects transactional with respect to audited turn acceptance. A player turn should not permanently mutate campaign/session/character state until the accepted candidate response is known.

Acceptance Criteria
- State-mutating gameplay tool effects from a candidate response are staged or wrapped in a rollbackable transaction until the turn auditor accepts that candidate.
- If the auditor rejects the candidate, all tool side effects from that rejected candidate are discarded before retry.
- If retry fails due to provider rate limit, provider error, auditor failure, invalid JSON, or retry-budget exhaustion, all candidate tool side effects from that player input are discarded.
- User-visible messages like "your last input was not applied" are true with respect to persisted gameplay state.
- Read-only tools may execute normally, but the system must have an explicit way to classify read-only vs mutating tools.
- Add regression tests covering:
  1. mutating tool executes, auditor rejects, retry succeeds: only accepted retry mutations persist
  2. mutating tool executes, auditor rejects, retry fails: no candidate mutations persist
  3. read-only tool execution does not require staged mutation handling
- Debug/session traces should make it clear whether a tool call was staged, committed, or rolled back.
- Do not solve this by disabling native MCP tools or by trusting model self-reporting.

Implementation Notes
Likely approaches include:
- transaction/savepoint around candidate tool execution and audit acceptance
- staged mutation journal applied only after audit acceptance
- tool-executor wrapper that records and rolls back mutating operations

Prefer the smallest safe implementation that fits the current orchestrator/tool execution architecture.
notes:
Investigation finding: the per-turn SAVEPOINT (TURN_SAVEPOINT) + per-attempt SAVEPOINT (ATTEMPT_SAVEPOINT) added in #241 (eshyra-oobh) ALREADY make candidate tool mutations transactional for ALL transports including the Agent SDK MCP path — a real-bridge probe confirmed reject+retry-success keeps only the accepted mutation, and reject+retry-fail (provider session limit) persists nothing. The 'applied=true' the operator saw is the tool RESULT, not proof of persistence; the SAVEPOINT discards it. The real gaps this bug exposed were (1) no explicit read-only vs mutating tool classification, (2) no staged/committed/rolled-back observability so an operator could not confirm the discard, and (3) the only MCP test fabricated tool results and never exercised the executeTool bridge, so the rollback guarantee was unproven for the path that actually runs MCP mutations.

Delivered: required Tool.mutates classification + ToolRegistry.isMutating (unknown=>mutating fail-safe); ExecutedToolCall.mutates threaded through all 3 transports + into the turn trace; TurnCandidateDispositionEvent (committed/rolled_back with reason accepted|audit_rejected|turn_error) emitted at every release/rollback point and persisted by the CLI file sink; regression tests via a faithful BridgeMcpModel covering reject+retry-success, reject+retry-fail (no persistence, no scene log, no trace), read-only-needs-no-staging, and disposition tracing. CLI 'your last input was not applied' fires only on result.ok===false (outer rollback) so it is true wrt persisted state.
close_reason: Merged via PR #244 (squash 4d7154a). Added required Tool.mutates classification + isMutating, ExecutedToolCall.mutates across all transports + turn trace, TurnCandidateDispositionEvent committed/rolled_back observability persisted by CLI sink, and real-bridge MCP regression tests proving reject+retry-success / reject+retry-fail rollback. SAVEPOINT transactional guarantee confirmed pre-existing and now proven for the MCP path.
